From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evan Torres <evan@procurex.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data terms edge cases — DPA redlines, SCCs, and sign‑off timeline

Hi Samir —

Thanks for sending Harbor Health's redlines over this morning. I reviewed the PDF quickly and flagged three things we should clarify before we send a formal redline:

- SCCs: Harbor has proposed custom wording that changes the controller/processor mapping in a few places (section 2.1/3.4). We think we can accept the spirit of the language but need to confirm whether they expect processing role changes across all subprocessors or only specific services.
- Data residency / export carveouts: they added an export carveout for research purposes and a requirement that all EU customer data be stored in EU unless explicitly agreed in the Order Form. We need product to confirm technical feasibility and an operations note on latency/cost impacts.
- TIA and evidence: Harbor's counsel is asking for a TIA addendum and a subprocessor whitelist. Operationally we usually provide subprocessor categories + SOC reports rather than a static whitelist.

I copied Evan (procurement) so he can confirm timing expectations. Can you put me in touch with Harbor's legal lead for a brief call if needed? I attached their redlines for reference.

Proposed next steps:
1) Legal (Laura) to propose a tracked-change redline for the DPA that keeps SCCs standard but accepts limited role clarifications.
2) Product/ops to confirm whether EU-only storage is feasible for this cluster and provide a delta estimate.
3) Sync call with Harbor legal (Dana) if there are open conceptual items after redline.

Goal: get a mutual action plan and target signoff window next week (preferably by 2028-06-25).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Harbor_HL_DPA_redlines_20280618.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir@harborhealth.com>

Cc: Dana Li <dana.li@harborhealth.com>, Evan Torres <evan@procurex.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data terms edge cases — DPA redlines, SCCs, and sign‑off timeline

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick read. A few clarifications from Harbor's side:

- The subprocessor whitelist request is meant to be narrowly scoped — our privacy team wants active visibility on any subprocessors that will be used to process PHI or other regulated data. We're open to a solution where Redwood provides a rolling notification + SOC attestation instead of a permanent whitelist.
- The EU‑only storage ask applies to patient data for EU residents; we can add carveouts where the customer explicitly opts out (e.g., cross-border research).
- The TIA request is a blocker for our procurement team — they need a tidy put-in-place plan or an equivalent mitigation (e.g., contractual commitments + periodic third‑party audits).

I'll loop Dana (Harbor Legal) in here. We can do a 30–45 minute call tomorrow (Tue) morning PT if that helps. Evan, can you confirm Harbor's procurement timeline and whether we have an exec commercial approval window?

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Sr. Director, Procurement
Harbor Health

Forwarding Harbor's initial redlines and Samir's reply. High level asks from Harbor: subprocessor whitelist (narrow), TIA addendum, and EU‑only storage for patient data. Procurement is eager to keep this moving — Harbor hopes to finalize by 6/25 if we can get an updated redline this week.

Can Legal draft a tracked-change DPA that:
- Preserves standard SCC language where possible,
- Adds a scoped clause for subprocessor visibility (suggestion: rolling notification + SOC attestation),
- Provides alternative language to TIA — either narrow TIA obligations or equivalent contractual attestation + SOC commitments,
- Includes a clean definition for "EU resident patient data" and Order Form tie‑in for storage geography.

Operational asks (for context):
- Is EU‑only storage realistic for a single-customer Order Form? If so, what is the cost delta and lead time? (I'll get product ops to respond separately.)

If legal can get a proposed redline by EOD Wed (6/20) we'll schedule a joint call with Harbor legal on Thu to run through outstanding items.

Thanks,
Kimberly

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data terms edge cases — DPA redlines, SCCs, and sign‑off timeline

Kim / Rishi —

Thanks for the context and the Harbor redlines. I've attached a tracked-change draft (Redwood_DPA_proposed_redline.docx) with the following recommended approach:

1) SCCs: Keep the standard EU SCC Annex as the base. Accept a targeted clarification in the MSA/DPA that specifies the functional roles for the specific Harbor services (e.g., ID mapping, telemetry). We should avoid wholesale controller/processor role changes.

2) Subprocessor visibility: Propose "rolling notification + 30‑day objection period for subprocessors used to process regulated data" language. If Harbor requires an immutable whitelist, we should ask for an express carveout and cost/lead-time to support a whitelist model.

3) TIA / evidence: We cannot commit to a broad TIA without an operational assessment. Offer a hybrid: contractual obligations (security commitments + right to audit) + annual SOC2 Type II + targeted TIA for a limited scope if Harbor pays for the assessment.

4) Data residency: Draft language that ties EU storage obligations to Order Form selections. Add operational acceptance criteria and an explicit lead time clause (e.g., 6–8 weeks to provision segregation).

5) Fall‑back and indemnities: Limit indemnity exposure tied specifically to Redwood's breach of security obligations; push back on open-ended cross-border liability.

Action items (suggested):
- Kimberly: confirm product/ops feasibility for EU‑only storage and provide cost/time estimate by EOD Wed 6/20.
- Rishi: commercial note on whether Harbor's ask for a whitelist requires a pricing uplift.
- Kimberly/Laura: if Harbor accepts rolling notification, proceed with updated redline and schedule call.

I'll be conservative with language where there is programmatic risk. If Harbor insists on an immutable whitelist or broad TIA at no cost, escalate to Legal Leadership for a principled exception.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts and Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_proposed_redline.docx

- TIA cost: if Harbor insists on a scoped TIA at Redwood's vendor, we should either pass-through the assessment cost or offer a hybrid discount in exchange for a longer-term commitment.

I'll join the call with Harbor on Thu 6/22 10:00 AM PT. Kimberly — please send the calendar invite once we confirm Dana's availability.
